iov_seachart_desc: A shard of an old Vegvisir, worn smooth by the sea. Use it to mark an islet nobody has visited yet on your map.
iov_seachart_found: The shard points across the sea: an islet is marked on your map.
iov_seachart_none: The shard stays silent: there is no unvisited islet left.
iov_beacon_lit: It burns. Its light shows the islets around it.
iov_beacon_need: To light the beacon you need: {0}
iov_beacon_flare: The beacon flares up... and something out there saw it.
iov_beacon_reward: The beacon's light shows the islets nearby. Marked on your map: {0}
iov_pouch_caught: Your hook brought up a sodden pouch: {0}
iov_trader_greet1: Ah... a sail. It has been long since a sail came this way.
iov_trader_greet2: Welcome, seafarer. Mind the planks, they're older than your grandfather's grandfather.
iov_trader_greet3: The tide said you would come.
iov_trader_bye1: May Rán keep her nets away from your keel.
iov_trader_bye2: Sail well. The sea remembers those who respect it.
iov_trader_bye3: Come back before the fog takes this place too.
iov_trader_trade1: Coin for craft. That is the old way.
iov_trader_trade2: These were my people's. Now they can be yours.
iov_trader_trade3: Look all you like, but don't drip on the goods.
iov_trader_buy1: Wear it well. It has sailed farther than you.
iov_trader_buy2: A fair trade. The sea approves.
iov_trader_buy3: A good choice. My grandmother swore by those.
iov_trader_talk1: My people built the towers you see on the islets. We lit the fires so others could find their way.
iov_trader_talk2: Once there were a hundred harbours like this one. Now there is mine.
iov_trader_talk3: The statue up there? One of our old captains. Nobody remembers his name. Not even me.
iov_trader_talk4: Watch the gulls. They know where the islets are.
iov_trader_talk5: Shards of our old Vegvisirs still turn up in the chests out there. They point the way, if you let them.
iov_trader_talk6: I don't buy. I have nowhere left to keep things.
iov_trader_talk7: Bára? She came in with the tide one day and never left. I named her after one of Rán's daughters, the waves.
iov_lure_desc: A carved lure of the old sea people. Fish on the islet fishing grounds take it readily, and the bigger ones come for it. Fish anywhere else ignore it.
iov_cape_desc: Oiled wool that keeps the spray and the night chill off your back.
iov_hat_desc: Every crew needs someone who looks like they know where they're going.
iov_vest_desc: Cut close, so it doesn't drag you down when you go over the side.
iov_trousers_desc: Tarred canvas. Water runs off it like off a gull.
iov_caulk_desc: Tar, oakum and a mallet. Use it on board to patch up your ship at sea, no workbench needed.
iov_caulk_done: You caulk the seams. Your ship is sound again.
iov_caulk_noship: You need to be on board a ship.
iov_stormmead_desc: Brewed for night watches in foul weather.
iov_ransblessing_desc: A mead for those who mean to go over the side. Rán lets them go... this time.
iov_saltedfish_desc: Keeps for a whole voyage. Tastes like one, too.
iov_hardtack_desc: Hard enough to break a tooth, filling enough to last until the next shore.
iov_se_hat_tooltip: You read the water like a captain.
iov_se_trousers_tooltip: Being wet wears off twice as fast.
iov_se_cape_tooltip: Keeps the night chill and the cold of the rain off you. Not enough against freezing cold.
iov_se_set_tooltip: The sea knows you: you never get wet, and you swim faster.
iov_se_storm_tooltip: Rain and spray don't soak you, and the cold doesn't reach you. Not enough against freezing cold.
iov_se_ran_tooltip: You swim faster and tire less in the water.
iov_storymap1_desc: A scrap of an old Brim sea chart, showing a harbour in the Meadows waters. Use it to mark the spot on your map.
iov_storymap2_desc: Ketill's course, torn from Sævar's charts. It ends in the Swamp waters. Use it to mark the spot on your map.
iov_piece1_desc: A piece of something old, warm to the touch. The sea doesn't want you to keep it.
iov_brimoil_desc: The Brim Folk kept their beacons burning with this. One flask lights any old beacon.
iov_stormglass_desc: Look through it and the sea seems to settle. It calms the water around you for a while, even when it's angry with you.
iov_ketill_intro: Come for my share, have you? Then take it from my neck.
iov_ketill_stage_1: Up, crew! Still want your share? Then earn it!
iov_ketill_stage_2: It's mine! Let the sea come and take it!
iov_ketill_death: Hrafn... I never raised your stone.
iov_story_mapped: The map shows a place somewhere around here.
iov_story_nomap: The map leads nowhere: this world has no such place.
iov_story_lit: The old harbour's beacon burns again. Sævar will want to know.
iov_sea_restless: The sea grows restless. It wants what you carry.
iov_story_q1_give: My people's first harbour lies in the Meadows waters. Its beacon has been cold for a lifetime. Light it, and I'll tell you who we were.
iov_story_q1_wait: The old harbour's beacon is still cold. I would feel it if it burned.
iov_story_q1_done: It burns... I saw it from here, for the first time in an age. Sit, and hear of the Brim Folk.
iov_story_q2_give: Ketill's crew sailed for the Swamp waters and never came back. Here is his course. Find what's left of them.
iov_story_q2_wait: Ketill's crew is still out there, in the Swamp waters. Bring me what they found.
iov_story_q2_done: So this is what Ketill found... Set it down. Gently. Listen, and I'll tell you what it did to them.
iov_story_later: The rest of the tale is still out at sea. Give me time to read the old charts.
iov_lore_brim_text:
We were the Brim Folk, and the sea was our field. We built our halls by the water and lit a beacon on every rock, so that no crew of ours would be lost in the dark.

Three crews sailed out each spring and came home each autumn: Ketill's, Sigrún's, and the boldest of them, Ormr's. What they found, they shared, and every hearth had its portion.

One autumn the sea would not lie still, though there was no wind. That was the year they brought home the light.

I was the last of us. When my days ran out, the halls of the slain would not open for me. So I wait here by the water, and keep the last beacon burning.
iov_lore_ketill_text:
Ketill was the first to find a piece of it: a sliver of something old that glowed like an ember and was never cold. He hung it about his neck and said it brought him luck.

It did, for a while. Then his crew began to count each other's shares. Then they began to quarrel over them. On an islet in the Swamp waters, with the sea roaring under a clear sky, they drew their blades.

None sailed home. Those who raised stones for the fallen were the next to fall, and what lies there now does not rest.

We shared what they sent us, all those years. Perhaps that is why the halls of the slain are shut to me.
iov_stone_harbour: Let you who read me know: here the Brim Folk lit their first beacon, so that no crew of theirs would ever be lost on the dark sea. Keep it burning.
iov_stone_ketill1: Hrafn raised this stone in memory of Úlfr, his brother. The sea took him on a windless day.
iov_stone_ketill2: Ketill raised this stone in memory of Ásgeirr, his oar-mate. He fell by a friend's hand.
iov_stone_ketill3:
Gold in the hold,
blood on the oar.
No one is left
to raise a stone for Hrafn.
iov_storymap3_desc: Sigrún's course, torn from Sævar's charts. It ends in the Plains waters. Use it to mark the spot on your map.
iov_storymap4_desc: Ormr's course, the longest of the three, torn from Sævar's charts. It ends in the Mistlands waters. Use it to mark the spot on your map.
iov_storymap5_desc: Sævar marked where the dvergr keep the fragment, in the Mistlands waters. Use it to mark the spot on your map.
iov_piece2_desc: Another piece of it, crusted with salt from years in a fish's belly. Still warm.
iov_piece3_desc: Ormr kept this one hidden. It has gone dark, as if it were holding its breath.
iov_piece4_desc: The dvergr carved runes around it, as if to keep it still. It isn't still.
iov_story_swallowed: Something glints in the fish's belly: {0}
iov_story_q3_give: Sigrún's crew went the other way, to the Plains waters. She was the wise one. Here is her course. If anyone threw that thing away, it was her.
iov_story_q3_wait: Sigrún's fragment is somewhere in the water around her islet. The fish there know more than I do.
iov_story_q3_done: From a fish's belly... Sigrún would have laughed. She gave it to the sea, and the sea gave it back. Sit. Hear how she tried.
iov_story_q4_give: Ormr sailed furthest, into the mist, and he cut his days into stone. Here is his course. Read what he left, and bring back what he hid.
iov_story_q4_wait: Ormr's islet is in the Mistlands waters. His stones will tell you more than I can.
iov_story_q4_done: He hid it from his own crew... and still it found them. But Ormr's bones weren't there, were they? Listen.
iov_story_q5_give: The dvergr have been asking about lights in the water. One of Ormr's fragments washed up at their outpost, and they keep it like a black core. Here is the way. They won't give it up, so be ready.
iov_story_q5_wait: The dvergr still have it. Take it, and they'll take it badly.
iov_story_q5_done: Four now. Four fragments, and the sea has never been so loud. They all pull the same way: south, to the burning waters. Hear what the dvergr knew.
iov_lore_sigrun_text:
Sigrún found the second piece in her nets, glowing among the fish. She saw how her crew looked at it, and how she looked at it herself.

On an islet in the Plains waters she called them all to the shore and threw it into the sea. The sea took it, but it was too late: the light had already taken them.

They fought until no one was left to fight. Sigrún was the last, and she raised no stone for herself.

A fish swallowed the piece and swam those waters for years, and no one knew why the sea there would not lie still.
iov_lore_ormr_text:
Ormr was the boldest of us, and the strongest of will. He found two pieces in the mist and hid them both, so that his crew would not quarrel as Ketill's had.

It did not save them. They felt it all the same, and turned on each other in the fog, and Ormr did not draw his blade. When it was over, he stood alone among them.

His bones are not on that islet. His stones say he heard someone calling him from the north, and that he answered.

The second piece he took with him. On the way the sea tore it from him, and the dvergr found it.
iov_lore_dvergr_text:
The dvergr pulled the piece from the surf and set it on a stand, as they do with the black cores. They studied it for a long time and wrote down what they learned.

It is older than their halls, they wrote, and it is not whole. Every piece pulls towards the others, and all of them pull towards one place, far to the south, where the sea burns.

There, they wrote, a woman once came ashore with her crew and found the thing whole. Her crew never left that shore.

The dvergr wrote her name only once, and then scratched it out.
iov_stone_sigrun1: Sigrún raised this stone in memory of Eydís, her steerswoman. The sea was calm; the hands were not.
iov_stone_sigrun2: Let you who read me know: here Sigrún gave the light back to the sea. Do not go looking for it.
iov_stone_sigrun3:
Thrown to the waves,
buried in the deep.
Whatever the sea takes
it gives back one day.
iov_stone_ormr1: I found two of them in the mist, lying in the shallows like lost coins. I told no one. I keep them under my cloak, and I sleep with my back to the wall.
iov_stone_ormr2: They know. They don't say it, but they count my steps. Last night Hálfdan asked me what I carry. I did not answer, and I did not draw my blade.
iov_stone_ormr3: They are all gone. I have locked one of them in my chest, where none of them can reach it now. The other lies warm against my heart, and someone in the north is calling my name. I am going.
iov_gullfeather_desc: Sigrún always wore one in her braid. Let it go into the wind, and the wind follows your sail for a while.
iov_se_tailwind_tooltip: While you sail, the wind is always at your back.
iov_harpoon_desc: The Brim Folk went after serpents with these. It bites deeper than any other harpoon.
iov_serpentcharm_desc: Serpent scale on a dvergr cord. Wear it and serpents bite softer, and the angry sea sends none after you.
iov_se_serpentward_tooltip: Serpents deal half damage to you, and the restless sea sends none.
iov_storymap6: Torn Map: Where the Sea Burns
iov_storymap6_desc: The dvergr's notes, copied onto Sævar's chart. They point to the Ashlands waters. Use it to mark the spot on your map.
iov_storymap7_desc: No one ever charted this place. Sævar drew it from where the fragments pull, deep in the Deep North waters. Use it to mark the spot on your map.
iov_piece5_desc: It lay in the ashes where it was broken, longer than anyone remembers. It is the warmest of them all.
iov_piece6_desc: The last piece, the one she kept. It is cold, as if it had finally let go of someone.
iov_story_ashes: The ashes stir. Her crew has not forgotten.
iov_arena_waiting: Something waits in this place, but not for you. Not yet.
iov_story_q6_give: The dvergr say south, where the sea burns. A woman found the thing whole there... Here, I copied their notes onto my chart. Whatever she became, she was a sailor once, like us.
iov_story_q6_wait: Her shore is in the Ashlands waters. Whatever is left of her crew is still there.
iov_story_q6_done: Hafdís... So that is her name. The sea's own guardian was one of us, once. Sit. This is the hardest page.
iov_story_q7_give: Five fragments, and now they all pull north, to where she keeps the last. Ormr is with her, and their son. Here is the way, as I drew it. Bring me that last piece, and this ends.
iov_story_q7_wait: The hidden islet lies deep in the Deep North waters. They won't let you take it easily.
iov_story_q7_done: All of it... Set it down with the others. Look, the light. It came for her once. Now it has come for me.
iov_lore_hafdis_text:
Long before the Brim Folk, a crew was cast ashore far to the south, where the sea burns. They made a life there. Their steerswoman was Hafdís.

One morning the waves brought a chest, and in it the thing, whole and shining. Hafdís put it on. Her skin fell from her like ash, and her crew came for her with knives. She killed them all.

Then a light came down from the sky, and when it was gone she was no longer only a woman. The sea was hers to keep, and the thing with it.

She broke it, because no one should carry it whole; its curse is the guard she set on it. One piece she left in the ashes, and one she kept. The rest she gave to the sea, and the sea gave them to us.
iov_lore_light_text:
Sævar set the last piece down with the others, and the light came down over the harbour, as it had once come down over Hafdís.

When it was gone, the pieces had become one small thing, clean and quiet. The sea did not stir.

Sævar was gone too. Two ravens circled once over his harbour, and flew away.

His chest still stands where he stood. Whoever comes by can trade with it, the old way: coin for craft.
iov_stone_hafdis1: The waves brought a chest this morning. In it lies something that shines like the first day of the world. I put it on. It is warm.
iov_stone_hafdis2: My skin falls from me like ash. They look at me the way men look at a burning house. Tonight they sharpened their knives.
iov_stone_hafdis3: They are gone, all of them. A light came down and spoke without words. I am to keep it. I will break it, so that no one carries it whole again.
iov_stone_hidden: Here they keep it, mother, father and son, so that no one else carries it. Turn back, unless you mean to take their place.
iov_grimr_spawn: Father said you would come. Mother said you would not leave.
iov_grimr_death: Mother... I kept it as long as I could.
iov_grimr_stage_1: Not yet. Mother still needs me.
iov_grimr_stage_3: You will not get past me to her!
iov_se_grimrchill_tooltip: Your limbs are stiff with cold.
iov_ormr_spawn: Sævar sent you. He always did count the shares.
iov_ormr_death: It's quiet... For the first time, it's quiet.
iov_ormr_stage_1: You hear them too, don't you? My crew... they never stop.
iov_ormr_stage_2: It feeds me. It always has.
iov_hafdis_spawn: You have carried five of them, and you are still yourself. So was he, once.
iov_hafdis_offer2: Stay. Keep it with me. The sea needs a guardian who does not break.
iov_hafdis_offer3: Or raise your hand against me, and carry it to the dead man in his harbour.
iov_hafdis_death: Then take it to him... and let the light decide.
iov_hafdis_stage_1: The sea does not let go of what it takes.
iov_hafdis_stage_2: Then let the sea itself judge you!
iov_brimheart_desc: What the light left of the fragments: small, clean and quiet. The sea knows whoever wears it.
iov_se_brimheart_tooltip: You swim faster and tire less in the water. Serpents deal half damage to you.
iov_ashtar_desc: Hafdís's crew tarred their hulls with this to sail the burning sea. Use it on board.
iov_se_ashtar_tooltip: The burning sea doesn't harm the ship you're on.
iov_call_text: Odin's eye was on the sea as Sævar walked toward the light. Now the old stones at his harbour have woken, and Sævar asks for you. Look for the light over the harbour.
iov_ringmaster_call: Are you the wanderer Sævar spoke of? Come here, talk to me, and challenge the Einherjar!
iov_ringmaster_won: Enough! The ring has seen you, and so have the Einherjar. You are one of us now, wanderer!
iov_valsaevar_won: The Einherjar have taken you in, and the Allfather saw it. My captains have come too, look: Ketill, Sigrún, Ormr and Grímr. They sit at the table, but they are not wholly here; each of them left something undone in the world. Speak with them.
iov_valsaevar_t3: All four of my captains are free; they truly sit at the table now. The rest of my people drowned with the curse on them, and Rán holds them in her net, where our fleet went down, far out in the Deep North's waters. Her beast keeps it: Hafgufa. I have drawn you the place. Tear the net, wanderer.
iov_valsaevar_t3remind: My people are still in Rán's net, among the masts of our fleet. Use the chart, and take a strong ship.
iov_valsaevar_t3done: I felt it when the net tore. They are coming, wanderer... soon this table will be full.
iov_t3_page_text:
Most of the Brim Folk drowned while the curse was on them, and Rán, whose sea it is, keeps the drowned in her net. Theirs lies where their fleet went down, far out in the Deep North's waters; the masts still stand out of the sea there.

Hafgufa, Rán's beast, keeps the net. While the net's three glowing knots float on the water nothing can hurt it: break them from your ship first.

Sævar's chart shows the way. Take a strong ship: Hafgufa can break a hull, but the drowned below will not let another ship go down there.

Tear the net, then return to Sævar in Valhalla.
iov_t3_map_desc: Sævar drew it from memory: where the Brim Folk's fleet went down, far out in the Deep North's waters. Use it to mark the spot on your map.
iov_t3_waiting: The sea here is heavy and still. Something waits beneath the masts.
iov_ran_rise: A voice from the deep: "Who sails into my net? Hafgufa, rise!"
iov_ran_shielded: Rán's net shields Hafgufa. Break the glowing knots first!
iov_ran_knotsbroken: The last knot breaks: Rán's net no longer shields Hafgufa!
iov_ran_net: A voice from the deep: "Then drown with them!"
iov_ran_hull: Rán's net wraps around your hull! Drowned souls come up out of the sea...
iov_ran_torn: The net is torn! The souls are rising...
iov_ran_free: A voice from the deep, softer now: "Take them, then. The sea forgets nothing... but this time, I let them go."
iov_t2_ketill_wish: Hrafn died because of me, and I fell before I could raise his stone. On my islet it still lies on the ground. Raise it, wanderer. Then come and tell me.
iov_t2_ketill_page_text:
Ketill's crew turned on each other on the islet in the swamp waters. Hrafn died because of him, and Ketill died before he could raise a stone in Hrafn's memory.

Go back to Ketill's islet and find Hrafn's unfinished stone. Raise it. Ketill's crew may not stand by and watch.

Then return to Ketill in Valhalla.
iov_t2_ketill_remind: Hrafn's stone still lies on the ground. Go back to my islet.
iov_t2_ketill_free: So it stands... Hrafn, brother. Now we can both rest.
iov_t2_ketill_thanks: The table has grown, wanderer. Thanks to you.
iov_t2_sigrun_wish: When the madness took me, I threw my sister's necklace into the sea. It was all I had left of her. You know what my stone says: whatever the sea takes, it gives back one day. Let that day be today.
iov_t2_sigrun_page_text:
Sigrún's crew met their end on the islet in the plains waters. When the madness took her, she threw her sister Ása's necklace into the waves.

Go back to Sigrún's islet and cast your line into her fishing ground. The sea may give the necklace back; but what comes up from the deep does not come alone.

Then return to Sigrún in Valhalla.
iov_t2_sigrun_remind: The necklace is still in the deep. Cast your line in my islet's waters.
iov_t2_sigrun_free: Ása's necklace... The sea kept its word. Now I can let go.
iov_t2_sigrun_thanks: One day I will see Ása again. You gave me that.
iov_t2_ormr_wish: There are words I never told my son. I carved them on my last stone, on my crew's islet, in the mist. Find it, read it... and take them to Grímr.
iov_t2_ormr_page_text:
Ormr carved his diary into stones while his crew turned on each other in the mist. No one ever read his last stone; the words he never told his son Grímr are there.

Go back to the islet of Ormr's crew and find the last stone. Seekers have nested close to it.

Then take the words to Grímr in Valhalla.
iov_t2_ormr_remind: My last stone is still waiting in the mist.
iov_t2_ormr_tellhim: So you read it... Don't tell me. Tell him. Tell Grímr.
iov_t2_ormr_free: My son heard. Now I can be silent.
iov_t2_ormr_thanks: I sit at the same table as my son. I owe that to a wanderer.
iov_t2_grimr_wish: My mother made me only one thing: a little wooden wolf. I left it in the north, on the islet where my father and mother waited for you, the day I began to keep watch. Bring it to me.
iov_t2_grimr_page_text:
Grímr spent his life guarding the treasure; he never got to be a child. His mother Hafdís made him something once: a little wolf carved from wood.

Go back to the islet in the Deep North, where Grímr and his parents waited for you, and find the toy. The creatures of the north may not have left it unguarded.

Then return to Grímr in Valhalla.
iov_t2_grimr_remind: My wolf is still in the north. Don't forget.
iov_t2_grimr_free: This is it... My mother's hands. Thank you, wanderer.
iov_t2_grimr_thanks: There is nothing left for me to guard. A strange feeling.
iov_t2_grimr_hears: My father wrote this? ... I heard you, father. I heard.
iov_t2_hrafn_text: Ketill meant to raise this stone in memory of Hrafn, his oar-brother; his life ran out first. A wanderer raised it in his stead.
iov_t2_hrafn_raised: Hrafn's stone stands. The swamp stirs...
iov_t2_sigrun_caught: Tangled in your line with the fish: a silver necklace. Ása's. Something stirs on the shore...
iov_t2_ormr_stone_text:
Grímr, if anyone reads this, let it be you.

Son, not once did I sit down and talk with you. My eyes were always on those cursed pieces, and I let your mother teach you to stand guard before you learned to play.

I watched you every day of it, and I was proud of you every day. I never said so. I am saying it now.

Put down your watch, son. It was never yours to keep.
iov_t2_ormr_stone_read: Ormr's last words. The mist stirs...
iov_t2_grimr_taken: Grímr's little wolf, worn smooth by a child's hands. The north is not letting it go quietly...
iov_bragi_won: I heard of your fight in the ring; I'm already setting it to a song. The wanderer who brought Starkaðr to his knee... that will make a fine verse.
iov_ringmaster_wait: Sævar is waiting for you at his people's table. Speak with him first.
iov_ringmaster_start: Then step into the ring, and show us what you are worth!
iov_ringmaster_again: Back for more? The ring is always open.
iov_duel_round3: Final bout: Starkaðr, champion of the Einherjar
iov_duel_won: The Einherjar raise their weapons to you: you have proven yourself worthy.
iov_duel_lost: You are beaten. Rest, and try again when you will.
iov_duel_fled: You left the ring. The bout is over.
iov_bragi_greet: Welcome, guest of the Allfather Odin. I am Bragi, and the songs of this hall are mine to keep. Sævar waits for you at his people's table, under the golden birches to the west.
iov_bragi_talk1: Every name sung in this hall was earned. Yours may be, too.
iov_bragi_talk2: The Einherjar fight by day and feast by night, and tire of neither.
iov_bragi_talk3: I have a verse for the Brim Folk already. It only lacks its ending.
iov_valsaevar_welcome: You came. I knew the light would find you. Listen, and I'll tell you what still holds my people.
iov_valsaevar_ring: The Einherjar wait for you at the ring. Speak with the Master of the Ring, and show them what Odin saw in you.
iov_rune_in1: Let you who read me know: you stand in Valhalla, the hall of the slain, the Allfather Odin's own. Few have walked here with breath still in them.
iov_rune_in2: On the fields of battle the valkyries choose the bravest of the fallen and bear them here. They are the Einherjar. By day they fight; at dusk their wounds close, and they feast.
iov_rune_in3: From his high seat, Hliðskjálf, the Allfather looks out over the nine worlds. His ravens, Hugin and Munin, fly where his eye does not reach, and tell him all.
iov_rune_in4: This path was laid for those the sea took. Walk it slowly, and remember them.
iov_rune_out1: You leave the hall of the slain, but its fires do not go out. They will burn until the end of days.
iov_rune_out2: Few walk out of Valhalla on their own feet. Fewer still are asked to come back. Be worthy of both.
iov_rune_out3: What the sea has taken, the sea may yet give back. Carry that with you over the waves.
iov_rune_out4: The Allfather watches the road behind you as he watches the road ahead. Go well, wanderer.
iov_guard_talk1: Keep your blade sheathed in the Allfather's hall.
iov_guard_talk2: We stand watch, as we will until the last day.
iov_guard_odin: The Allfather is not to be disturbed, wanderer.
iov_lore_scattered_text:
The curse is broken. Hafdís rests at last, and the sea no longer keeps what was never its own.

But the Brim Folk died cursed, and the cursed dead do not come to Valhalla. Rán took them into her net beneath the waves, and most of them are there still. Some never went even that far: they are bound to the places where they fell, by what they left undone.

Odin has promised me this: when my people are gathered, they may come home, at peace. I cannot do it alone. I belong to this hall now, and the sea is no longer mine to sail.

But first, the Einherjar want to see what kind of guest Odin has brought. Go to the ring, and show them.
